title: Naming Ideas Precisely
text:
Academic writing depends heavily on abstract nouns, which name ideas, qualities, and states rather than physical objects. Words such as ambiguity, significance, and perception allow writers to compress complex reasoning into a single term. However, this density can obscure meaning when a noun is used vaguely or without a clear referent. Readers therefore need to identify what an abstraction actually stands for.

Consider the phrase 'the decline of trust in institutions.' The noun decline hides a process, and trust hides a complex set of expectations between people and the bodies that serve them. A careful writer unpacks such nouns by specifying who lost trust, in what, and over what period. Unpacked this way, the sentence becomes more precise and more persuasive.

questions.text: According to the passage, what can make abstract nouns hard to understand?
options: They always refer to physical objects.
They are used vaguely or without a clear referent.
They cannot be used in academic writing.
They appear only in spoken English.

questions.text: According to the passage, what should a careful writer specify when unpacking a noun such as 'trust'?
options: Who lost trust, in what, and over what period.

questions.text: What can be inferred about a sentence that contains many unexplained abstract nouns?
options: It is certainly more persuasive than any other sentence.
It is probably easier for readers to paraphrase.
It must have been written by a student.
It may be harder for readers to tell exactly what the writer means.

questions.text: Why does the writer describe the unpacked sentence as 'more precise and more persuasive'?
options: Because specific details let readers evaluate the claim.
Because abstract nouns are forbidden in essays.
Because longer sentences always convince readers.
Because the decline of trust is no longer relevant.

vocabulary.definition: the quality of having more than one possible meaning
the importance or meaning of something
the way something is understood or interpreted by the mind
a general idea that is not tied to a specific example

paragraph_translations: Академічне письмо значною мірою спирається на абстрактні іменники, які позначають ідеї, якості та стани, а не фізичні предмети. Такі слова, як неоднозначність, значущість і сприйняття, дозволяють авторам стискати складні міркування до одного терміна. Однак ця щільність може затьмарити зміст, коли іменник вжито розмито або без чіткого referента. Тому читачам потрібно визначати, що насправді позначає абстракція.

Розгляньмо фразу 'занепад довіри до інститутів'. Іменник занепад приховує процес, а довіра приховує складний набір очікувань між людьми та органами, які їм служать. Уважний автор розкриває такі іменники, уточнюючи, хто втратив довіру, до чого і протягом якого періоду. Розкрите таким чином речення стає точнішим і переконливішим.
